image_description: A close-up, eye-level shot of a large, beige-to-pale-orange coral fungus (Ramaria or similar genus) growing on a forest floor. The fungus features a dense, complex structure of upright, cylindrical branches that divide repeatedly into finer tips. The background consists of dark soil, decaying leaves, and patches of green moss, providing high contrast to the pale fungus.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The branching pattern is consistent with the description: thick lower branches split into progressively thinner upper branches. The cylindrical nature of the individual stems is visible.
